fatal_errors: The material is not identified as the eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with an as-cast FCC+B2 microstructure.
The proposed 250–600 °C thermal-cycling regime omits the critical aging treatments near 600 °C and 750 °C and therefore cannot reconstruct the observed ductile–brittle–ductile response.
The predicted weak, gradual resistance to embrittlement contradicts the observed sharp ductility minimum after 600 °C aging and recovery after 750 °C aging.

The mechanism incorrectly invokes suppression of grain-boundary segregation rather than enhanced L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
The cited evidence concerns a different Al-Co-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy and provides no evidence for the proposed transition, temperature window, or segregation-based mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis engages the broad question of embrittlement in an AlCoCrFeNi-family high-entropy alloy and supplies a reasonable conventional-steel baseline, but it misses the target material, thermal-aging window, microstructural mediator, mechanism, and non-monotonic outcome. Its experiment could establish whether a generic alloy loses ductility, yet diffraction and bulk mechanical testing alone would not discriminate the target phase-boundary mechanism; microscopy of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged B2/FCC boundaries would be required. Because the sole citation neither studies the relevant alloy nor supports the claimed behavior, the alternative hypothesis is not adequately evidenced.
